subject: Renewal: Request to add reserved GPU pools in EU + APAC
messages:
From: Tim Morales <tim.morales@novacorp.com>

Cc: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@novacorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T10:02:00Z
Subject: Renewal & Dedicated Expansion: request to add EU+APAC pools

Hey Karthik,

As we approach our renewal (contract ends 2026-04-15), we want to lock in additional reserved capacity in EU and APAC rather than relying on burst in the US. Our usage in Q1 spiked in EMEA and APAC and the latency to our EU customers is starting to impact real-time features.

High level ask: add dedicated reserved pools in Dublin (EU) and Singapore (APAC) as part of the renewal. Target start aligned with renewal date.

Rough numbers from our side (current prod peak):
- EU: 8 concurrent inference workers needed for 99th-p95 p50 mix, rough target 90–110 req/s sustained across business hours.
- APAC: 5–6 workers, peak ~60–80 req/s.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood provision reserved GPU pools in EU & APAC with throughput guarantees / 99th percentile latency targets?
2) What's the failover behavior if one region loses capacity?
3) Pricing and options for committed term (we're open to 24-month commit for a better rate).

Attached: usage_export_q1.csv (sample telemetry and regional breakdown). Please route to whoever owns Dedicated renewals and infra SLOs.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Morales
Head of Platform — NovaCorp
[Attachment: usage_export_q1.csv (CSV)]

Karthik — quick pricing + offer notes (high level):

Option A — 12-month commit
- EU pool: 8 reserved A100-equivalent vCPU/GPU slots; baseline throughput guarantee = 100 req/s sustained (with auto-burst to 150 for short durations).
- APAC pool: 6 reserved; baseline throughput guarantee = 70 req/s sustained (burst to 110).
- Term: 12 months, standard renewal pricing.
- Discount: standard reserved capacity discount (12%).

Option B — 24-month commit (preferred for NovaCorp pricing)
- EU: same capacity, 24-mo pricing at 18% discount.
- APAC: same, 18% discount.
- Includes one cross-region failover license and 10% monthly burst buffer shared across pools.

Commercial caveat: committed throughput measured at request/sec and normalized token consumption — we'll need to baseline with your telemetry (the CSV helps).

Let me know if we should add a package for higher SLA (p99 latency SLO, 99.95% availability) — that's a separate premium.

--Lauren

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-03-19T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal & Dedicated Expansion: request to add EU+APAC pools

Internal technical notes for proposal — paste into the commercial doc:

Sizing assumptions (based on Tim's CSV + our perf profiles):
- EU (8 reserved A100 equiv): expected steady-state 85–110 req/s depending on payload; 99th-p latency target ~120–160ms for standard generation calls (seq len ~256).
- APAC (6 reserved): steady 55–80 req/s; 99th-p ~140–180ms.

Failover behavior options:
1) Active-active: traffic balanced across regions; if one region degrades, traffic shifts gradually (we maintain sticky prefixes + geo-proximity). Pros: lower user latency pre-failure; cons: more reserved capacity overall.
2) Active-passive (recommended for cost): Primary in region, passive cold standby in failover region with automated prefix promotion and KV cache warming. Expected failover time ~90–180s depending on model warmup; we can shorten to ~30–60s with pre-warmed instances (adds cost).

Throughput guarantees & degraded-mode behavior:
- Guaranteed throughput is bounded by reserved pool capacity. We'll specify request/sec pledges and provide burst windows.
- For cross-region failover, we recommend a small shared burst pool (10% of combined reserved) to avoid immediate throttling during cutover.

Operational hooks to include:
- Canary routing rule, automatic fallback to hosted API for non-sensitive traffic, and healthchecks with automatic alerting to NovaCorp SRE.

I'll include expected ingress/egress metrics to surface in the MAP so procurement can size network.

Sergio
Principal Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime

Tim — attaching our proposed configuration and pricing (summary below). If this aligns, we'll cut commercial paperwork and route to DocuSign for signature. Suggested effective date: 2026-04-15 (renewal).

Proposal summary (attached: redwood_dedicated_renewal_proposal_v2.pdf):
- EU pool (Dublin): 8x reserved GPU-equivalents; baseline throughput guarantee = 100 req/s; 99th percentile latency target ~120ms; active-passive failover by default; optional pre-warmed failover for <60s cutover.
- APAC pool (Singapore): 6x reserved; baseline throughput guarantee = 70 req/s; 99th p latency ~140ms.
- Shared burst buffer: 10% of combined capacity for cross-region spikes.
- Term & pricing: 24-month preferred — 18% reserved capacity discount vs list; 12-month option available at 12% discount.
- SLA: 99.95% availability on reserved pools (payouts per SLO table in attachment).
- Add-ons: higher p99 latency SLO (premium), additional pre-warmed failover, extended support.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred term (12 vs 24 months) and any premium add-ons.
2) We provide final commercial redline; we’ll route to DocuSign (link below) for legal/procurement.
3) Technical onboarding plan — Sergio/Evelyn will coordinate a 2-week cutover window and test plan.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/ABC123-sign
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_renewal_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF)

Best,
